The delete-catching branch itself is proven by P2's offline repro (stand-in resource, plan.md P2 record) since provoking a real delete/replace against a live prd VM is exactly what the slice exists to prevent and was not attempted. The commit copy ran cleanly (rc 0) against a real no-op prd plan.json in this pass.

items.description: The apply job stays the operator's tool for creating and removing VMs, with no guard override (F1 ruling). After a VM is destroyed on Proxmox, neither Terraform's refusal nor the guard stops the plan that recreates it. Once its vms.tf entry is gone, neither stops the plan that deletes its non-VM companions, such as its DNS reservation (terraform/modules/managed-vm/main.tf:39): both rails act on the VM resource only (terraform/modules/managed-vm/main.tf:52).
items.rationale: Static design fact, verified by reading: the guard's jq filter keys on `.type == "proxmox_virtual_environment_vm"` only, and prevent_destroy sits in the lifecycle block of that same resource, not on homelab_dns_reservation.this (a separate resource in the module). Neither rail therefore touches the DNS reservation delete that follows a vms.tf entry removal. No override flag exists in either script or Jenkinsfile. Not live-tested (would require actually removing a real VM's companion resources against prod), consistent with V11 being operator-owed for the end-to-end path.
evidence: support/iac-agent/bin/check-protected-vms.sh:36-38 — filter keys on type == proxmox_virtual_environment_vm
terraform/modules/managed-vm/main.tf:39 — homelab_dns_reservation.this, a separate resource from the VM
terraform/modules/managed-vm/main.tf:208-214 — lifecycle{prevent_destroy} sits on proxmox_virtual_environment_vm.this only
grep of Jenkinsfile.iac-apply/-on-push/-scheduled-drift and check-protected-vms.sh: no override/skip flag anywhere

items.description: "add prevent_destroy" — as ruled (D1): prevent_destroy is on the VM resource in the shared managed-vm module (terraform/modules/managed-vm/main.tf:52, lifecycle block at :208). That covers every prd VM, with no module split and no state move, so a plan that would destroy or replace any prd VM fails, in Jenkins or locally. It fails at plan time (Error: Instance cannot be destroyed; terraform plan exits 1), so every job stops before terraform show and the guard (Jenkinsfile.iac-apply:71, Jenkinsfile.iac-on-push:45, Jenkinsfile.iac-scheduled-drift:183-184). terraform/scratch is unaffected.
items.rationale: Verified live against real infrastructure, safely and read-only (terraform plan, no -out, no apply): a forced-replace plan against the real srviac VM was refused by Terraform itself with exactly the documented error, before reaching check-protected-vms.sh. terraform/scratch has its own resource and its lifecycle block is untouched by this diff.

This pass, live: `cexec iac terraform plan -replace='module.vm["srviac"].proxmox_virtual_environment_vm.this' -no-color` against the real terraform/prd (no -out, nothing applied) → "Plan: 1 to add, 0 to change, 1 to destroy." then "Error: Instance cannot be destroyed ... Resource module.vm[\"srviac\"].proxmox_virtual_environment_vm.this has lifecycle.prevent_destroy set, but the plan calls for this resource to be destroyed."

items.description: "checked plan ≠ applied plan" / "single iac invocation applying the saved plan" — iac-apply plans, runs the guard and applies that saved plan inside one iac invocation, in one stage. The plan file never leaves the container, and a plan Terraform refuses, or one the guard fails, applies nothing. Today Jenkinsfile.iac-apply:60-77 plans and checks, then :79-90 re-plans and applies in a fresh container (:10-11). Live proof is one operator run of iac-apply.
items.rationale: Statically verified: Jenkinsfile.iac-apply's "Terraform plan + destroy check + apply (prd)" stage is one `iac -c` call running init, plan -out, show -json, check-protected-vms.sh and apply of the saved .tfplan under set -e, matching P3's offline shell-level repro (create/no-change/replace-refused/guard-rc1/guard-rc2/late-resource cases, plan.md P3 record). Deliberately not run live here: iac-apply converges real prd (site.yml, site-openbao.yml, site-k8s.yml, an actual terraform apply) — that is exactly the operator's keystroke this slice does not change, and it would also currently fail at the same stale-srviac-guard usage error as V02/V10 until A1 is done.
evidence: Jenkinsfile.iac-apply: one stage, one `iac -c '...'` running terraform init, plan -out=/tmp/plan.tfplan -detailed-exitcode, show -json, check-protected-vms.sh /tmp/plan.json, terraform apply -input=false -no-color /tmp/plan.tfplan

plan.md P3 record: offline repro of this exact stage body (awk-extracted) against a local Terraform config — create, no-change, refused-replace, guard-rc1, guard-rc2 and late-resource-added cases all behaved as designed
Owed command: operator runs the `IaC/Apply` Jenkins job (manual-only, no trigger) — only after A1 (srviac's guard reinstalled), or it fails at the same usage error build #164 hit

items.area: R1 — drift job guard result and protected-VM signal
items.description: "drop `|| true` in drift job" — the drift job no longer swallows the guard's result (Jenkinsfile.iac-scheduled-drift:181). As ruled (plan review r1, 2026-09-14), Terraform's plan-time refusal is the protected-VM signal: a refused VM delete or replace names itself in the drift job's build description instead of reading as ordinary drift. Today driftSummary's resource-header match (Jenkinsfile.iac-scheduled-drift:82) and items ?: errors (:106) would record it as module.vm["srvX"].proxmox_virtual_environment_vm.this must be replaced. A VM left tainted by a failed create (docs/runbooks/vm-rebuild.md:135) takes this path on every daily run.
items.rationale: Statically verified and now also confirmed against the real refusal's exact text (this pass's V04 live check): driftSummary's refusal regex `Resource\s+(\S+)\s+has\s+lifecycle\.prevent_destroy\s+set` matches the live srviac error's wrapped "Resource module.vm[\"srviac\"]...this has\nlifecycle.prevent_destroy set" text verbatim. The `|| true` is gone from the drift job's guard call. What remains unproven is the Groovy itself running under the real Jenkins CPS sandbox (Matcher.find(), recordDrift, currentBuild.description) — no JVM is reachable from this pod; P6 review r1 already proved both Jenkinsfiles parse (CompilationUnit.compile). Live proof needs a real drift build that hits a refusal, which this pass deliberately did not provoke (drift is read-only by design, but forcing a refusal into the scheduled job means editing vms.tf, out of scope for a read-only test pass) — it settles on the daily 11:00 schedule once a refusal or the operator's own drift trigger occurs, or sooner if the operator runs `IaC/Scheduled-Drift` by hand.
evidence: Jenkinsfile.iac-scheduled-drift: prdCheck() calls the guard with no `|| true`; driftSummary()'s terraform branch matches `check-protected-vms:` lines and the prevent_destroy refusal regex before drift items
This pass's V04 live output: "Resource module.vm[\"srviac\"].proxmox_virtual_environment_vm.this has\nlifecycle.prevent_destroy set" — matches the regex's wrapped-address shape exactly

items.description: "a failed SSH host-cert stage aborts iac-scheduled-certs before either leaf stage runs" — every stage of iac-scheduled-certs runs whatever an earlier stage did, and the build still goes red if any prd stage failed. Today its stages are plain declarative stages with no catchError (Jenkinsfile.iac-scheduled-certs:78-164).
items.rationale: Statically verified: every prd stage now runs its playbook through prdStage(cost, shellScript), which uses sh(returnStatus:true) then catchError(buildResult:'FAILURE', stageResult:'FAILURE') around error() on a non-zero exit — the sh call itself sits outside catchError so an abort still stops the build, and stages after a failed one still execute (declarative `stages` runs each stage in sequence regardless of an earlier stage's FAILURE result once it's set via catchError rather than an uncaught throw). No JVM/Jenkins is reachable from this pod to execute the Groovy; P6 review r1 already proved both Jenkinsfiles parse. Live proof is the job's own next scheduled run.
evidence: Jenkinsfile.iac-scheduled-certs: def prdStage(cost, shellScript) { ... catchError(buildResult: 'FAILURE', stageResult: 'FAILURE') { error(...) } }; "Host certs (excl. k8s dev)" and "TLS leaves (excl. k8s dev)" both call prdStage(); no stage-level post{failure}
Owed: `IaC/Scheduled-Certs`'s next Friday 04:00 run, or an operator-triggered run, ideally with a forced failure to exercise the path

items.description: When several stages fail, their build descriptions are combined rather than the last overwriting the others. Today certs assigns at Jenkinsfile.iac-scheduled-certs:91,160 while drift appends at Jenkinsfile.iac-scheduled-drift:129-138. A stage that passed adds no entry, and no entry claims that a later stage did not run when it now does (certs :91).

Both only fire on a stage's own non-zero exit — a passing stage adds nothing. The old "TLS leaf renewal did not run" wording is gone from certs per the plan's done-record and confirmed absent by grep.

items.description: "a dev-stage failure in iac-scheduled-certs loses its Telegram warning when a later prd stage then reds the build" — in both scheduled jobs the dev-stage warning is raised at the point the dev stage fails, once per failure, not only from post { unstable } (Jenkinsfile.iac-scheduled-certs:208-220, Jenkinsfile.iac-scheduled-drift:403-412). It therefore reaches Telegram whatever the final build result. notify.warning only writes a log marker (/work/JenkinsPipelineUtils/vars/notify.groovy:46-48), and the bot raises every marker in a finished build's log (/work/DockerImages/jenkins-telegram-bot/app/bot.py:136-137,142-165).
items.rationale: Verified by reading both Jenkinsfiles: each dev stage that fails (non-devUp() skip aside) calls notify.warning(...) inline at the point of failure, then unstable(...); there is no longer a post{unstable} block or DEV_STAGE_FAILED variable in either file, so a later prd FAILURE cannot suppress a dev warning that already fired. JenkinsPipelineUtils' notify.warning and the telegram bot's per-marker scan were read to confirm the marker reaches Telegram independent of final build result (unchanged by this slice, cited for completeness).
